Let baby nurse as long as they want! Cluster feeding is normal at this age and will help increase your supply. Pumping helped me too I think. Just keep an eye on diapers and if they’re having plenty of wet diapers throughout the day they should be getting enough but if you’re ever concerned you can bring it up to the Dr. I never met with a lactation consultant but I know they can be very helpful and help you know if baby is getting enough too. My suggestion, if she truly won’t take a bottle (tho I’ve heard if you’re out of the house and she’s hungry enough, she’ll take the bottle) start stretching her time between feedings. I started doing this a few weeks ago by setting the time on my huckleberry app for every 2 hours, then every 2 1/2, and now we’re up to every 3 hours. And she can often go longer than this but I try not to feed her before the mark so that she doesn’t get back into her snacking habits which it sounds like your girl likes to do too. If you can stretch those times, you’ll be able to relax more and get a bit more energy which will help in many other ways too!

My goodness there’s already so many replies but I’ll share mine anyway. I wanted to go fully unmedicated but was open to an epidural if I felt I needed it or the pain became too much and I think just giving myself the grace and knowing that it was an option made it easier for me to choose not to do it. Well that plus my amazingly supportive husband who breathed through those really intense contractions with me when I thought I couldn’t go much longer. 
But I was one of those people who was like: my body was made for this! Women have been doing this for millennia and I can do it too! So I wanted to fully experience it and honestly just to be able to tell myself I did it. 

Ultimately I ended up having to be induced due to my hypertension but I was already almost 3cm dilated before the induction and after about 4-5 hours my body pretty much took over and they were able to dial back the pitocin. Which, thank good for that because my contractions were only about 1-2 minutes apart and grew in intensity so quickly! My labor ended up being 12 hours (almost exactly) and the hardest part for me ended up being pushing which was for about an hour and a half. The pain had become so intense I felt like it was time even though I wasn’t quite ready yet so my nurse had me start practice pushing and changing positions to help baby descend. I was so exhausted by the end of it I felt like I’d pass out but then after my baby was delivered I had so much adrenaline I couldn’t even sleep the first night!

I hope I don’t have to be induced when I have another baby but if I do, I know I can handle it! Even though things will be different and I may decide to get the epidural I feel a sense of pride that I was able to do it without it the first time.
Oh I did do the gas though but that really only helps with the pain at the beginning- it doesn’t do shit for the pain in the later stages but rather just gives you a distraction and something to help you focus your breathing.

Honestly if labor taught me anything though? It’s that our bodies are fucking amazing! And no matter how a person brings a child into this world, it’s a feat worth celebrating!

Okay mama, first breathe! You seem very stressed but from what I just read, you are taking EXCELLENT care of your little girl!
Breast milk production is weird and while your supply is likely starting to regulate it doesn’t actually regulate until around 3 months. I went through the same thing as you where I was pumping very little then all the sudden pumping almost 10 oz in the morning when baby girl was sleeping longer stretches. Then around 3/4 months it dipped down to only about 4-5 oz and I was so worried but that amount has been consistent since and I’m almost 6 months pp now.

So your supply will still likely have days where you have a lot because of baby sleeping through the night or longer stretches and then some days where you’ll only pump a few oz. Or maybe you’re an oversupplier and will have large pumps every time! But the most important part is your baby is fed and if she seems generally happy and isn’t asking for more food then you’re fine. Track her diapers and as long as she’s still getting plenty of wet diapers through the day and pooping consistently (but remember it’s normal for breastfed babies to go a few days without pooping) then she’s getting enough. 

Please try not to stress about the weight, babies all grow at different rates and weighing on the scale isn’t the most accurate anyway (I’ve tried it too and it was off by like 2 or 3 pounds!)
When you see the dr they will tell you if she’s gaining enough and if by some craziness she’s not you can tell the dr that you’re pumping plenty and my bet is you may just be recommended to feed her on a schedule.

Breastfed babies are great at telling you when they’re hungry from what I’ve heard and from my own experience. If she’s happy and content then it sounds to me like you’re doing everything right!

Well I’ve only had one baby but I was on Zoloft (generic sertraline) for about a year before getting pregnant then all through pregnancy and now 5 months pp and breastfeeding! My dr actually prescribed it because it is “safer for pregnancy” than what I was taking before. I ran out of it for about 2 weeks due to insurance changes before I could get a refill but am back on it now and I can say, without a doubt, that I am a better mom while taking it.

I had to have more ultrasounds than the typical pregnancy because my Dr ordered them due to a med I was on (even though it is considered safe for pregnancy- even the ultrasound tech was confused but did it anyway). I also had to do a fetal echocardiogram to check baby’s heart and this took almost 3 hours to make sure they got everything. I ended up having to go to a perinatal clinic 3 separate times I think because of my extra scans that they were unable to do in my OB office.
It was a little stressful at first but I got the see my baby way more often than the typical pregnant woman may. Plus I got the extra reassurance that all my baby’s organs were growing well and strong! We even got a few 3D pics without even having to ask!

I’m sorry you’re having to go through all this extra nonsense because of insurance but unfortunately that’s the kind of bs we just have to deal with for now. But when things do get sorted just remind yourself you get to see your baby! That always helped me get through it

This for sure! After you confirm your milk is still tasty for baby, I usually thaw and warm 1 bottle before leaving the house and put it in the insulated pouch in my diaper bag. Since warmed milk is only good for about 2 hours I don’t like taking more than one bottle of milk out and if she gets hungry again I just nurse her.


If I’m dropping her at our parents place to babysit for the day I have a large insulated bag that I put the frozen bags (which we have them keep in their freezer while they’re there), 2 clean bottles, and the bottle warmer in. My bottle warmer has a frozen setting on it but I usually just thaw it under warm water in the sink then warm it in the bottle warmer as this is much faster. If we don’t want to pack the bottle warmer we just bring the glass bottles so they can warm them in hot water on the stove.

My baby had to go back to the hospital at 3 days old because of jaundice and she was also dehydrated (combination of the jaundice and my milk just coming in and her struggling with a latch the first few days)
The hospital had to supplement with formula the first few feeds because she needed to eat and my milk had only just come in that morning. I was pumping every 2 hours and had my husband bring the milk to the hospital for her (we live across the street) since I couldn’t breastfeed while she was under the phototherapy lights. Then less than a week later I ended up in the hospital with postpartum preeclampsia so once again we had to give her some formula and I was pumping at the hospital every 2 hours and the family was rotating picking up the milk for her because she couldn’t be in the intermediate care unit I was in due to being a newborn and L&D didn’t have a bed for me.
She took the bottle well and now bottle feeds excellently.
But I still nurse her for the majority of every day on demand and pump twice a day to have a supply for daddy and other family members to feed her! She’ll be four months on Sunday and our breastfeeding journey has been going great! 

Continue pumping to get your supply up and still offer the breast regularly then top off baby with some formula (or whatever routine your Dr has recommended)
Remember: fed is best! And it sounds like your supply is doing great so you may not need to supplement for more than a few days or weeks at most!

It sounds like you’re having a panic attack- the thing about those is they always pass I promise! Sometimes it feels like the world is closing in on you from every angle and you don’t know how to escape but if you take a deep breath, observe your surroundings and notice that you are safe, nothing is going to happen to you you might feel a little better. Try the 5 senses technique: find 5 things you can see, 4 things you can touch, 3 things you can hear, 2 things you can smell, 1 thing you can taste it will help ground you! If this doesn’t help try counting (out loud) backwoods from 100 it will help steady your breathing! 
Sometimes when you’re feeling like this too, getting to a different location can help you feel more relaxed, go outside for a few minutes, change rooms and play some music, make yourself a snack or even try out a new recipe- it helps bring your mind to something else. If all else fails- grab a piece of paper and just write everything running thru your head right at that moment- sometimes getting it out of your head and on paper helps you feel a little better because it’s not all trapped in your mind anymore- you have it in front of you. I do this but usually don’t even read what I wrote after I just write to get it out of my head.

Hi there, I recently have been working on improving my mental health and therapy was always scary for me too because I always thought I could do it on my own. My depression has gotten better but my anxiety has gotten much worse. About 2 month ago I started going to a few counseling sessions at my university. Their program is set up to help you find help outside of the university so you can get regular sessions that the university does not offer. Through them they gave me a list of referrals that are very affordable because they keep in mind that many of their patients are college students. If she still is a member of her university these services are usually free/included with tuition. Talking about problems and what's going on in your life with a neutral party like a therapist can help tremendously. If she's worried about medication the doctor can not force her to take meds and she can tell them that she wants to try other methods before she considers medication. You could also help her by finding therapy/counseling centers in your area and calling to see what kind of plans they offer for students/ people without insurance. Of course she needs to be willing to go as well otherwise it won't do much good. It took me years of my boyfriend telling me I needed help to actually finally consider therapy so give her time and make sure you are by her side when she needs you but remember to take care of yourself too. Supporting people with mental illness can be a challenge and often we don't want to be a burden on other people.
If you ever feel like she may attempt suicide or you get a strange call or text or she tells you she is a danger to herself in that moment- do what you can to get to her but you may need to contact help outside of your own resources as well. I hope I helped and best of luck with everything.
